text:
Andrei Svechnikov went seven goals in a ten-game stretch this month, including back-to-back two-goal nights against Seattle and Edmonton, and the Hurricanes kept winning around him. He has 13 goals in 25 games, ten power-play points, and 54 hits, which tells you how he plays.

Some of the scoring is borrowed. He's shooting 18.8%, above the 15% our numbers think is his real level, and Carolina has scored 4.7 more goals than its chances deserve with him on the ice. Two goals in his last five games, both in one night, suggests the hot streak is already cooling.

What's real: Carolina gets 61% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with him out there, and Evolving-Hockey had him 94th percentile among forwards for creating offense last season. The same source flags the cost: opponents got more chances with him on the ice too, bottom 6% of forwards defensively. He's 26, a Stanley Cup champion, and on a deep team that doesn't need him to carry it. Our range has him at 29 to 43 goals.
